title: ED Allergy Communication Gaps for LEP Patients
summary: Learn how ED teams can capture allergy history for patients with limited English proficiency, including substance, reaction, severity, timing.
body_markdown:
###


Use language support to ask for the substance, reaction, severity, timing, and source of the allergy history instead of stopping at a yes-or-no allergy question.


###


“No known allergies” means a usable history was obtained and no allergy was identified. “Unable to obtain” means the team still lacks reliable information.


###


Family can contribute useful history, but when the patient can participate, professional language support gives the clinician a direct channel to the patient.


###


Later information from the patient, family, pharmacy, prior records, or medication review may clarify or contradict the first entry.


###


Yes. AI medical interpretation can support rapid allergy clarification when the language is supported and communication remains clear, with another method available if uncertainty persists.
